summary.headline: Kotyark FY26 revenue Rs 314.9 crore, EBITDA Rs 48 crore, PAT Rs 19.4 crore, at only 7-8% capacity utilisation after Rajasthan expansion to 1,500 KLPD.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 314.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 48 crore and PAT of Rs 19.4 crore while running at roughly 7-8% capacity utilisation. The Rajasthan biodiesel plant was expanded from 500 KLPD to 1,500 KLPD, taking cumulative annual capacity to about 4,80,000 KL. Management cited an executable order book of about Rs 80 crore and a pipeline of about Rs 215 crore, and announced two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar and Kanpur due by December 2026. Management guided utilisation to rise towards 60-70% over several years, with near-term growth of 15-20% stated. Several answers were vague or inconsistent, and the call did not provide quarterly figures or a specific capex amount.

segments.name: Biodiesel (OMC and industrial)
segments.commentary: Rajasthan (Sirohi) capacity raised from 500 to 1,500 KLPD; cumulative capacity about 4,80,000 KL per year. Management says industrial sales are rising after ARAI certifications, and the company has three plants: two in Padgol, Gujarat and one in Sirohi, Rajasthan.

segments.name: Glycerin and byproducts
segments.commentary: Management cited glycerin as a byproduct monetised across pharma, food, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue figures were given.

segments.name: FMCG
segments.commentary: Analyst asked about recently launched FMCG products; management said they are doing well across all markets, with no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Utilisation to improve gradually towards 60-70% over the next few years, per management.
Near-term growth of 15-20%, possibly up to 30%, with at least 15% expected; management said revenue and utilisation growth would be roughly in line.
Management said margins would improve a little as utilisation rises, but gave no quantified margin target.

Two new 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar (Haryana) and Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh) expected to be commissioned by December 2026, adding 400 KLPD (about 75% increase in capacity per management), funded from internal accruals.
Management targets 60-80% growth over the next four to five years.

Biodiesel exports: management said an export licence would take four to six months, with a Padgol or Sirohi unit converted to an EOU and ISCC certification pending; the call gave conflicting timelines and export revenue was said to arrive 'this year'.
risks_watch: Margin compression: the analyst cited a drop from about 15% to 8-10% operating margin; management did not reconcile the two figures.
Utilisation at 7-8% against a 1,500 KLPD plant and the 400 KLPD expansion; growth depends on OMC tenders and industrial demand.
Policy risk: an isobutanol blending plan was mentioned by the minister; management called it unviable on price and said the government favours ethanol.
Legal matters: the promoter's seized-raw-material case (next hearing next month) and the Supreme Court penalty matter with no timeline; a Rajasthan registration renewal is pending.
Export timing is unclear: management gave a 4-6 month licence timeline and also said revenue would arrive 'this year' and in Q1; ISCC certification is still pending.

Governance and disclosure: management declined a factory visit and some answers were evasive or unclear (asset turnover, employee plans); promoter share sales were described as being used to reduce debt towards zero-debt.
Feedstock: management said it uses 10-15 non-edible feedstocks and does not use used cooking oil (UCO).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, but vague and sometimes inconsistent on specifics such as margins, export timelines, utilisation and asset turnover, which management deferred. Management was defensive on policy questions and declined to comment on the isobutanol plan.
key_quotes: We are also setting two new biodiesel manufacturing facility at Jhajjar in Haryana and Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh, each with a capacity of 200 KLPD.
Management remains confident of improving utilization level gradually over the next few years towards 60 to 70%.
Kotyark Industries achieves a yield of more than 99%, and that is also one of our strengths.
No, I am reducing debt. I am taking the company towards a zero-debt position.

qa_highlights.question: Why are OMCs not increasing biodiesel tender quantity and blending despite higher crude prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it depends on government policy and OMC requirements and blending will keep rising gradually.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current operating margin given the move in OMC rates, and why did it fall from about 15% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current margins are 8-10%, that raw material cost moves with OMC rates so the margin is unchanged, and that it manages costs so PAT is not significantly affected; it did not reconcile the 15% figure.

qa_highlights.question: Will revenue and utilisation grow by 15-20%, and will margins hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue and utilisation growth would be roughly in line at 15-20%, possibly up to 30%, with at least 15% expected; margins would improve a little as utilisation rises.

qa_highlights.question: When can exports start and will revenue come in FY27 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the export licence takes four to six months, one of the Padgol or Sirohi units would be converted to an EOU, and ISCC certification is pending; it said export revenue would come 'this year itself'.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asset turnover expected at the Sirohi plant at normal utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an asset turnover figure; it gave Rs 3,500-4,000 crore as the revenue at optimum utilisation and said it would explain asset turnover later.

qa_highlights.question: Is the promoter share sale being used to fund the new plants, and what is the debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the proceeds stayed in Kotyark, it took nothing personally, and the sale was to reduce debt, with the aim of a zero-debt position.

capex_capacity: Rajasthan (Sirohi) biodiesel capacity raised from 500 to 1,500 KLPD in FY26; cumulative annual capacity about 4,80,000 KL; management expects utilisation to rise gradually to 60-70% over next few years from current 7-8%.

Two new 200 KLPD biodiesel plants at Jhajjar (Haryana) and Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh), total 400 KLPD, expected commissioning by December 2026; management said this is about a 75% capacity increase; funded from internal accruals.

No capex amount disclosed for the Jhajjar and Kanpur plants; management said plant cost is about one-fourth of peers' Rs 250-300 crore investment for 300-350 KLPD plants, but gave no figure for the new projects.
Existing storage judged sufficient; no additional storage or depot plans; company uses own vehicles for finished goods delivery.
Management declined a factory plant visit, offering an office visit instead.
demand_pricing: Demand driver cited: OMC blending tenders; analyst said an earlier tender ran at about 5 crore litres per month and a current tender for 15 crore litres over three months has been issued, and asked why OMCs are not raising blending; management said it follows government policy and OMC requirements and will increase gradually.
OMC tender allocation has moved from location-based to total-quantity-based; management said the company only needs to fulfil quantity, and previously it bid in locations where it was not L1.

Pricing: management said raw material cost moves with OMC rates, so a lower rate leaves margin unchanged; at current rates operating margin is 8-10% (analyst had cited about 15% in FY26; management said margins have improved in industrial sales without disclosing price).

Industrial demand: management said industrial sales are rising after ARAI certifications for mining and generator operators; industrial diesel reportedly around Rs 140 per litre per analyst, price not disclosed by management.
Customers named by management: sells biodiesel to Modern Insulators and semi-finished biodiesel to E-Diesel Biofuels; management said it can supply raw or semi-finished material to competitors.

Exports: management said biodiesel export is currently banned and a licence is being obtained; the company needs one of its Padgol or Sirohi plants converted to an EOU and ISCC certification, which is in process.

Glycerin: management cited monetisation across pharmaceuticals, foods, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue numbers given. Vera carbon certification with over 57,000 carbon credits generated.
Order book: executable order book of about Rs 80 crore from OMCs and other customers, expected to execute over the next three months; pipeline of about Rs 215 crore.
Feedstock: management said it uses 10-15 non-edible oils and does not make biodiesel from used cooking oil, citing higher cost and lower yield.
Geography: current focus is North India; management said it may later expand to Maharashtra; no plans for southern expansion stated.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue/volume growth of 15-20% (at least 15%, possibly up to 30%), backed by an executable order book of about Rs 80 crore expected to execute over three months and 400 KLPD of new plants due by December 2026, but utilisation is only 7-8%, no capex figure was given, and the export and margin timelines were inconsistent.
